title: The Drop of Water
summary: Old Krible-Krable was an eccentric philosopher who spent his life peering through powerful magnifying lenses at the microscopic world....
full_text:
Old Krible-Krable was an eccentric philosopher who spent his life peering through powerful magnifying lenses at the microscopic world.

One afternoon, he dipped a glass slide into a murky ditch-puddle, placed it under his great microscope, and invited his friend to look.

Thousands of tiny, fierce creatures swam and wrestled within the single drop of water! They bit off each other's limbs, swallowed one another whole, and fought furiously over every microscopic speck of weed.

"What a monstrous, bloodthirsty city this must be!" gasped the visitor. "Look at those generals conquering their neighbors, and those mobs tearing down their fellows!"

"It is no great city of men," laughed old Krible-Krable with a wry smile. "It is merely a single drop of ditch-water! Yet how like the great capitals of human pride it appears, where mortals fight and rage over fleeting trifles, blind to the vast universe that arches above them!"
moral: Looking upon human strife through the lens of wisdom reveals the pettiness of selfish conflict.
